name: findmy-cli
description: OpenClaw plugin for macOS Find My friend locations. Read-only and consent-bounded: it reads only the friends who have already opted in to share their location with this Mac's Apple ID, returns coarse location only, and cannot surface anyone who has not consented. For personal use locating consenting friends and family, not surveillance. Shells out to the findmy CLI to drive FindMy.app via screen capture and Vision OCR. macOS-only. Install findmy first via `brew install omarshahine/tap/findmy-cli`.
//: openclaw is the HOST runtime, not something this plugin ships. It belongs in
peerDependencies -- openclaw's own packaging guide prescribes exactly that
(docs/snippets/plugin-publish/minimal-package.json) -- and is marked optional so
npm does not auto-install a copy of the host into a consumer's tree. Declaring it
under `dependencies`, as this package did until 2026-09-01, put openclaw's entire
dependency tree in this repo's lockfile at RUNTIME scope and attributed every
advisory in it to this repo: 23 open Dependabot alerts for code no consumer of
findmy-cli ever installs.
The top-level `import { definePluginEntry } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry'`
in src/index.ts still resolves at runtime: OpenClaw refuses to npm-install a
registry copy of the host into a managed plugin project (a stale host copy corrupts
peer resolution) and instead reasserts a plugin-local node_modules/openclaw link for
packages that declare the host peer. See openclaw docs plugins/dependency-resolution.md.
The devDependencies entry is here for TYPES and nothing else. definePluginEntry is a
typed import, so `npm run typecheck` fails with TS2307 without it (and `api` in
src/index.ts degrades to implicit any). It is NOT needed to build -- tsup externalizes
the peer -- and NOT needed by `plugin:ci`, which runs the inspector with --mock-sdk;
both were verified to pass with openclaw absent. Managed installs run
`npm install --omit=dev --omit=peer`, so neither entry reaches a consumer.
Do not move openclaw back into `dependencies`.
